items.title: Jim Cullum interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2007
items.q: I was able to interview a fellow who was a child actor in the original production of “Porgy and Bess.” His name is Al Tinney.

ctx.x: Well yeah it was great. I had the idea to do “Porgy and Bess” and, because I love that music, and the farther I went into it I said I want to do the whole opera, and that sort of distinguished it from every other pop or jazz version that had ever been done. Because Louis and Ella and Miles Davis and the various ones that existed were all highlights versions. We did the whole opera. We did every song in the whole opera. And then I wrote this narrative that followed the plot. And so then we recorded it and we…

Wow. That’s saying something. I was able to interview a fellow who was a child actor in the original production of “Porgy and Bess.” His name is Al Tinney. He became a jazz © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -14-
piano player. But apparently he said he used to sit and play piano duets with Gershwin you know.
